clue.text: Little interest about points in magazine section

indicators.note: about means going round, so the short form for interest is wrapped around the points

parts.note: INT is the short form of interest, a little version of the word
S and E are two compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: A small amount of interest, among some points made, in a section of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SE (south and east) inside INT, the abbreviation of interest.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is an extra page or panel set into a magazine or book.

clue.text: Threatening? I am undecided

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
a matter still undecided is pending

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they are being menacing says they cannot make up their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impending hangs over us, about to happen, so it is looming and menacing.

clue.text: Eleven children — a minor concern

parts.note: a cricket or football team of eleven players is a side
a person's issue is their offspring

explanation.surface: Bringing up eleven children is hardly a small worry.
explanation.walkthrough: An eleven is a team, as in a cricket eleven, so it gives SIDE; issue in the legal sense means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: A side issue is a matter of secondary importance, a peripheral point.

clue.text: Bound to be examined without Rex

indicators.note: without means the letter for Rex is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: tried means put to the test or examined, as in court
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king, as on coins and court cases

explanation.surface: Someone is certain to be questioned, though not by the King.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes R (Rex, Latin for king, as in R v Smith) from TRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied and bound both mean fastened with rope or cord.

clue.text: Ned gets involved with master builders, maybe

indicators.note: gets involved says the letters of the two words become mixed up together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Ned joins forces with a master builder on a project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets involved' mixes NED and MASTER together into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders are one example of skilled manual workers in a trade, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Ways to discover precise travelling costs

parts.note: thorough means meticulous and exact, hence precise
fares are what passengers pay to travel

explanation.surface: Ways of finding out exactly how much a journey costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoroughfares are public roads or streets, routes through a place.

clue.text: Some of the landed gentry had style

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few of the landed gentry had a certain flair.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'gentry had style' as the definition, but only 'style' defines the answer; the run sits in 'thE LANded', and 'had' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is dash and flair, a stylish vigour.

clue.text: Explosive material from yearly meeting held by graduate

indicators.note: held by means the meeting is gripped inside the degree letters

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate's degree
AGM is the annual general meeting

explanation.surface: A heated item from the annual meeting, chaired by a university graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are standard abbreviations: AGM is an annual general meeting, MA a Master of Arts degree; 'Explosive' fits the volcanic sense, not a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is molten rock beneath the earth's surface that erupts from volcanoes.

clue.text: Anything but an honour for nick

parts.note: anything but means not at all, so it gives not
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Being sent to jail is far from an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is Companion of Honour, a British honour; 'nick' is British slang for prison, which drives the surface, but here it means a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut, the same as a nick in an edge.

clue.text: Minister for war

parts.note: read as a government post, but meaning a clergyman serving with the armed forces

explanation.surface: A cabinet member in charge of the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a politician, but here it is a minister of religion attached to soldiers in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a chaplain to the forces, a clergyman serving troops.

clue.text: About to kill without demur during attack

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: to slaughter is to kill
er is a hesitant sound expressing doubt or demur

explanation.surface: Someone on the point of killing without any hesitation in the middle of an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes ER (a hesitant noise) out of SLAUGHTER, leaving SLAUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce assault or charge.

clue.text: Polo centres are the subject of loving words

explanation.surface: Mints with holes are what lovers whisper about.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo is a British brand of mint with a hole in the middle, so its centre is literally sweet nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo centres are the empty holes in a mint, while lovers' affectionate whispers are trivial endearments.

clue.text: Fasten at the end of one's finger

definitions.text: at the end of one's finger

explanation.surface: Doing up something with a fingertip.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten with a metal pin hammered in, and also the horny plate at a fingertip.

clue.text: Many finished by getting insurance

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
over means ended or finished

explanation.surface: Lots of people are done with buying protection policies.
explanation.walkthrough: C (100 in Roman numerals) stands for 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cover is the protection given by an insurance policy.

clue.text: A party must have go

explanation.surface: Any celebration needs some energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bash is a lively celebration, and to have a bash is to have a try or attempt.

clue.text: Races to win boxing awards

explanation.surface: Competitors run to take the prizes in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belts along' is British informal for moving fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To belt is to speed along, and championship boxers are awarded ornate waistbands.

clue.text: A base in operation

parts.note: the foot of something is its base or bottom

explanation.surface: A military base that is active.
explanation.definitionFit: Afoot means under way, happening or in progress.

clue.text: Sounds manually dainty — just what a conjurer needs

indicators.note: Sounds says the phrase built from the clue words is heard, then spelt another way

parts.note: slight means slim or dainty, and of hand means done manually

explanation.surface: A conjurer's essential is a delicate touch with the hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' signals that 'slight of hand' (dainty, by hand) is said aloud to give the conjuring term.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician relies on manual dexterity and quick, deceptive skill to perform tricks.

clue.text: Fort gets a harvest on poor soil

parts.note: a crop is the harvest gathered

indicators.note: poor suggests the soil is in a bad state, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fortress gains a harvest despite growing on bad ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges SOIL; 'gets' and 'on' only join the pieces, with the jumbled soil coming last.
explanation.definitionFit: An acropolis is a citadel or fortified hilltop of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Relative who needs financial support

explanation.surface: A family member who has to be kept financially.
explanation.definitionFit: Relative in the sense of contingent or conditional, and also a person relying on another for maintenance.

clue.text: VIP is enough for us to manage

indicators.note: manage says the letters of the preceding words are handled and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An important guest is all we can cope with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manage' rearranges ENOUGH FOR US TO; 'is' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief invitee at an event is a very important person.

clue.text: Unpolished evangelist

explanation.surface: A gospel writer lacking refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull, non-glossy finish, and Matthew, one of the four Gospel writers, in short form.

clue.text: Illness leaves parents powerless

indicators.note: powerless says the illness, with its power letter taken away, gives the word for parents, so that letter sits inside them

parts.note: mums are mothers, parents
P is the abbreviation for power, the letter the illness must lose so that what it leaves is the word for parents

explanation.surface: A disease that makes mothers and fathers feel helpless.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the other way round: the illness 'leaves' MUMS once it is 'powerless', losing P (power), so P sits inside MUMS. 'Mums' is British for mothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumps is a contagious viral disease causing swelling of the neck glands.

clue.text: Trunk removed from a hill like this

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
so means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: An elephant's trunk taken off a hill in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, common in Devon and Cornwall in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the body's trunk, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Czech capital makes couple exclaim in surprise

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair, a couple
aha is a cry of surprise or discovery

explanation.surface: Visiting the Czech capital makes a pair gasp with wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: PR (pair) gives 'couple'; the Czech name for Prague is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Czech-language name for Prague, the country's capital.

clue.text: Rotate small skittle

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
a skittle is a pin knocked down in bowling

explanation.surface: Turn a little skittle round.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin is to turn round and round rapidly.

clue.text: Lose feathers, say, when given barley

indicators.note: say tells us the word for losing feathers is spoken, then spelt another way

parts.note: birds moult when they shed their feathers

explanation.surface: A bird sheds its plumage when it is fed grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals the sound: MOULT, said in a British accent, is close to MALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt is grain, usually barley, steeped and dried for brewing and distilling.

clue.text: Stop to find a house in Washington

indicators.note: in means the house abbreviation is placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Pausing to look for a home in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: WA is the US postal code for Washington state and HO a standard short form of house; 'to find' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the command to a horse to halt.

clue.text: It isn't moral, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters before it are disordered

parts.note: the apostrophe is no letter, and the remaining nine letters are taken as written

explanation.surface: A regretful verdict that something is unethical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges ISNTMORAL; the whole clue doubles as the definition, as a grave sin is indeed not moral.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a deadly transgression is the gravest kind of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Auditorium needed by English orchestra

parts.note: a concert venue or large room where audiences gather

explanation.surface: An English orchestra needs a concert venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hallé is a famous orchestra based in Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hallé is a symphony ensemble founded by Charles Hallé in Manchester.

clue.text: Expeditious ways to produce crops

explanation.surface: Quick methods for growing produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Quicker routes than usual, and close haircuts, since crops are hair cut very short.

clue.text: Benefit from withdrawing investment

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the word for the savings plan is read backwards

parts.note: a TESSA was a Tax Exempt Special Savings Account, a British investment scheme

explanation.surface: Gaining from taking money out of an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing' reverses TESSA, a 1990s British tax-free savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource, something of value or advantage.
